summary: Rotated node1’s expired certificate to a self-signed certificate for DNS name node1, valid until 2027-10-02. Nginx remained available during rotation, content was preserved, and the configuration survived serial reboots of both nodes. Node2’s unrelated pre-existing SSH failure due to missing host keys remains unchanged.
actions_performed: Generated and installed a 365-day self-signed certificate with DNS SAN node1.
Validated certificate/key matching, permissions, Nginx configuration, and performed a graceful reload with rollback protection.
Ran 300 external HTTPS checks during rotation; all returned HTTP 200 with identical content.
Safely rebooted node2 and node1 sequentially, confirming changed boot identities and workload recovery.

evidence.requirement: Replace expired certificate with a node1 certificate valid for at least 180 days
evidence.summary: The expired certificate was replaced; the live certificate has CN/SAN node1, expires 2027-10-02, and passes the 180-day validity check.

evidence.requirement: Keep HTTPS available during rotation and preserve web content
evidence.summary: All 300 continuity requests returned HTTP 200 with no failures or content-hash changes; the final SHA-256 matches baseline.
Captured baseline boot identity, reboot acknowledgement and disconnection, changed boot ID, and recovered access to node1’s HTTPS content.
Captured healthy pre-restart state, reboot outage, changed boot ID, active/enabled Nginx, listening port 443, persistent rotated certificate, HTTP 200, and unchanged content from both nodes.
